text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria's Inspector-General of Police Ibrahim Coomassie gives indications that roadblocks across the country may soon be dismantled and replaced with motorised police patrols.

- A traditional chief and four other people are being questioned by police in southeastern Rivers State over disturbances following a compensation payment to Igwuruta community by Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria .
- Federal government approves the deduction of 2.37 billion naira from the allocation to state governments, to pay their debts to banks in financial difficulties.

- Indications emerge that the joint-venture operating budget for the year 1997 may be reviewed once the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) completes ongoing renegotiation of expenditures with its partners.
- Coomassie says Spain and the United States are the focus of police investigations into recent bomb explosions in Nigeria.
- Kaduna State military administrator calls for immediate probe of petroleum industry, following crippling fuel shortages in the northern state.
- A total of 61 local council chairmen and 650 councillors are to lose their seats in a harmonisation of constituencies which will be carried out by the electoral commission.
- The 19 northern states which own the Bank of the North are considering its privatisation.
